questions.question: Which of the following is the largest freshwater lake in India?
questions.explanation: Wular Lake in Jammu & Kashmir, formed by tectonic activity on the Jhelum River, is regarded as the largest freshwater lake in India. Chilika is the largest brackish-water lagoon, Sambhar is a saltwater lake, and Loktak in Manipur is famous for its floating phumdis but is smaller.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens, laid down in Article 51A of the Constitution, were inspired by the constitution of which country?
options: A) Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR)
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and the idea was borrowed from the constitution of the erstwhile USSR. The USA influenced fundamental rights and judicial review, and Ireland influenced the Directive Principles.

questions.question: Who founded the Maurya Empire in ancient India around 322 BCE?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya, with the guidance of his minister Chanakya (Kautilya), overthrew the Nanda dynasty around 322 BCE and founded the Maurya Empire. Bindusara was his son and successor, Ashoka was his grandson, and Samudragupta belonged to the later Gupta dynasty.

questions.question: The headquarters of the International Labour Organization (ILO), a specialised agency of the United Nations, is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The ILO, founded in 1919 under the Treaty of Versailles, has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. It became the first specialised agency of the United Nations in 1946. New York hosts UN headquarters, while Vienna and Paris host other international organisations.

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey, which laid the foundation of British political power in Bengal, was fought in which year?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the forces of Robert Clive of the East India Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, who was defeated partly because of the conspiracy involving Mir Jafar. The Battle of Buxar (1764) consolidated British power, while 1761 is associated with the Third Battle of Panipat.

questions.question: Which classical dance form of India traces its origins to the temples of Odisha and draws heavily from the devotional tradition of the Maharis of the Jagannath temple at Puri?
questions.explanation: Odissi, one of the oldest surviving classical dance forms, originated in the temples of Odisha and was historically performed by the Mahari dancers dedicated to Lord Jagannath at Puri. Its characteristic tribhanga posture and sculptures of Konark and Sun temples reflect its Odia roots. Kuchipudi is from Andhra Pradesh, Mohiniyattam from Kerala and Manipuri from Manipur.

questions.question: The Chola emperor Rajendra I sent a celebrated naval expedition across the Bay of Bengal in the 11th century against which Southeast Asian kingdom?
questions.explanation: Around 1025 CE, Rajendra Chola I launched a naval expedition against the Srivijaya Empire, which controlled trade through the Malacca and Sunda straits from its base in Sumatra (present-day Indonesia). The campaign secured Chola influence over maritime trade routes. The Khmer Empire flourished in Cambodia, Majapahit rose in Java only after the Chola expedition, and the Pagan Kingdom was in Myanmar.

questions.question: The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris. Which city will host the 2028 Summer Olympics?
questions.explanation: The 2028 Summer Olympics will be held in Los Angeles, USA. The 2024 Olympics were in Paris, and the 2032 Olympics will be in Brisbane.

questions.question: Which country won the ICC Men's T20 Cricket World Cup in June 2024, ending a wait for an ICC title stretching back to 2013?
questions.explanation: India won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024, co-hosted by the West Indies and the USA, defeating South Africa by seven runs in a tense final at Bridgetown, Barbados. It was India's first ICC trophy since the 2013 Champions Trophy. England were the defending champions but were eliminated earlier, and Australia lost in the Super Eight stage.

questions.question: The 2024 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to which South Korean writer, honoured for her 'intense poetic prose that confronts historical traumas'?
questions.explanation: Han Kang of South Korea won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Literature, becoming the first South Korean laureate in the category. She is known for works such as 'The Vegetarian' and 'Human Acts'. Can Xue (China) and Gerald Murnane (Australia) were frequently cited contenders, and Salman Rushdie is a Booker-winning British-Indian novelist who has not won the Nobel.

questions.question: The 38th National Games of India, held in January-February 2025 after a gap of more than a decade, were hosted by which state?
questions.explanation: The 38th National Games were hosted by Uttarakhand from 28 January to 14 February 2025, across cities such as Dehradun, Haldwani and Rudrapur, and were branded as the 'Green Games'. Goa had hosted the 37th edition in late 2023, and the previous such games had been held in 2015 in Kerala.

questions.question: The 2024 Booker Prize was awarded to Samantha Harvey for which novel, written from the perspective of six astronauts aboard the International Space Station?
questions.explanation: Samantha Harvey won the 2024 Booker Prize for 'Orbital', a slender novel that follows six astronauts over a single day in orbit and reflects on Earth's fragility. 'The Safekeep' by Yael van der Wouden, 'Held' by Anne Michaels and 'Creation Lake' by Rachel Kushner were among the other titles on the 2024 shortlist.

questions.question: In December 2024, India's D. Gukesh became the youngest undisputed World Chess Champion in history by defeating which reigning champion in the title match held in Singapore?
questions.explanation: Gukesh Dommaraju, aged 18, defeated China's Ding Liren 7.5-6.5 in the World Chess Championship match held in Singapore in November-December 2024, becoming the youngest undisputed world champion, breaking Garry Kasparov's record. Magnus Carlsen had voluntarily given up the title in 2023, and Nepomniachtchi and Caruana were earlier title contenders.

questions.question: In January 2025, ISRO achieved a milestone by carrying out its 100th launch from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota. Which launch vehicle performed this mission, carrying the NVS-02 navigation satellite?
questions.explanation: The 100th launch of ISRO was achieved on 29 January 2025 by the GSLV-F15 rocket, which placed the NVS-02 satellite, the second generation navigation satellite, into orbit using the indigenous cryogenic upper stage for the 100th mission. PSLV-C58 (January 2024) carried XPoSat, LVM3-M4 launched Chandrayaan-3 in 2023, and SSLV-D3 carried EOS-08 in August 2024.

questions.question: Find the next term in the series: 4, 9, 19, 39, 79, ___
questions.explanation: Each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by 2 and adding 1: 4×2+1 = 9, 9×2+1 = 19, 19×2+1 = 39, 39×2+1 = 79. Hence the next term is 79×2+1 = 159.

questions.question: Pen : Writer :: Scalpel : ?
questions.explanation: A pen is the characteristic tool used by a writer; similarly, a scalpel is the characteristic tool used by a surgeon. Hospital is a place, not the user of the tool, a wound is acted upon, and a scalpel is not a nurse's defining tool.

questions.question: In a certain code, each letter of a word is replaced by the letter sitting at the same distance from the opposite end of the alphabet, so that A is coded as Z, B as Y, C as X, and so on (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, ...). If SUN is coded as HFM in this code, how will MOON be coded?
questions.explanation: Under the opposite-letter rule, the letter at position n from the start is replaced by the letter at position (27 − n). Using the given example: S(19) ↔ H(8), U(21) ↔ F(6), N(14) ↔ M(13), confirming SUN → HFM. Applying the same rule to MOON: M(13) → N(14), O(15) → L(12), O(15) → L(12), N(14) → M(13), giving NLLM.

questions.question: Three of the following four numbers are perfect cubes of natural numbers. Which one is NOT?
questions.explanation: 8 = 2³, 27 = 3³ and 125 = 5³ are perfect cubes, whereas 100 = 10² is a perfect square and is not the cube of any natural number, since 4³ = 64 and 5³ = 125. Hence 100 is the odd one out.

questions.question: P is the father of Q. Q is the wife of R. S is the son of Q and R. T is the brother of Q. How is T related to S?
questions.explanation: Q is S's mother, and T is the brother of Q. The brother of one's mother is one's maternal uncle, so T is S's uncle. R is S's father and P is S's maternal grandfather, so the other options describe different relatives.

questions.question: Starting from her house, Divya walks 6 km towards the east. She then turns to her left and walks 8 km, turns left again and walks 6 km, and finally turns left once more and walks 2 km. How far is she now from her house, and in which direction from it?
questions.explanation: Take the house as the origin. Walking 6 km east, then 8 km north (left of east), then 6 km west (left of north) cancels the eastward leg, leaving her 8 km north. A final left turn at this point faces her south, and walking 2 km reduces the northward offset to 8 − 2 = 6 km. She is therefore 6 km north of her house.

questions.question: Find the next term in the series: 1, 4, 13, 40, 121, ___
questions.explanation: Each term follows the rule ×3 + 1: 1×3+1 = 4, 4×3+1 = 13, 13×3+1 = 40, 40×3+1 = 121. The next term is 121×3+1 = 364. Equivalently, the terms are (3ⁿ − 1)/2 for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

questions.question: The price of a textbook rose from ₹250 to ₹300. What is the percentage increase in its price?
questions.explanation: Increase in textbook price = 300 − 250 = ₹50. Percentage increase is calculated on the original price: (50 / 250) × 100 = 20%.

questions.question: The average of four numbers is 15. If three of the numbers are 10, 14 and 20, what is the fourth number?
questions.explanation: The sum of the four numbers is 4 × 15 = 60. The sum of the three given numbers is 10 + 14 + 20 = 44. The fourth number is therefore 60 − 44 = 16.

questions.question: In a college class of 60 students, the ratio of boys to girls is 2 : 3. How many girls are there in the class?
questions.explanation: The ratio 2 : 3 divides the class into 2 + 3 = 5 equal parts. Each part is 60 ÷ 5 = 12 students. Girls correspond to 3 parts, so there are 3 × 12 = 36 girls (and 2 × 12 = 24 boys).

questions.question: A dealer sells a second-hand bicycle for ₹2,640 and earns a profit of 10% on the cost price. What was the cost price of the bicycle?
questions.explanation: Selling price = cost price × (1 + 10/100) = 1.1 × cost price. So cost price = 2640 ÷ 1.1 = ₹2,400. Option A comes from incorrectly subtracting 10% of the selling price, and C and D are near-miss values.

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 240 km in 4 hours. If it maintains the same average speed, how far will it travel in 7 hours?
questions.explanation: Speed = 240 ÷ 4 = 60 km/h. In 7 hours the car covers 60 × 7 = 420 km.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 10 hours and pipe B can fill the same tank in 15 hours, while pipe C alone can empty the full tank in 30 hours. If all three pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how long will the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: In one hour, A fills 1/10, B fills 1/15 and C empties 1/30 of the tank. Net filling rate = 1/10 + 1/15 − 1/30 = (3 + 2 − 1)/30 = 4/30 = 2/15 of the tank per hour. Time to fill = 15/2 = 7.5 hours.

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 8% per annum is ₹64. What is the sum?
questions.explanation: For 2 years, the excess of compound interest over simple interest equals P(r/100)². Here P × (8/100)² = 64, so P × 0.0064 = 64, giving P = 64 ÷ 0.0064 = ₹10,000. Check: SI = 10,000 × 0.08 × 2 = ₹1,600; CI = 10,000 × (1.08² − 1) = ₹1,664; difference = ₹64. ✓

questions.question: A and B invest ₹12,000 and ₹18,000 respectively in a business. A is a working partner and receives 10% of the profit for management. If the total profit is ₹15,000, how much does A receive?
questions.explanation: A's management share = 10% of 15,000 = ₹1,500. Remaining profit = ₹13,500. A's investment share = 12,000/(12,000+18,000) = 12/30 = 40%. A's share of remaining = 40% of 13,500 = ₹5,400. Total A receives = 1,500 + 5,400 = ₹6,900.

questions.question: The area of a square plot is 144 square metres. What is the perimeter of the plot?
questions.explanation: Side of the square = √144 = 12 m. Perimeter of the square = 4 × side = 4 × 12 = 48 m.

questions.question: Riya thinks of a number. When she multiplies it by 2 and adds 3, she gets the same result as when she multiplies the number by 3 and subtracts 5. What is her number?
questions.explanation: Let the number be x. Then 2x + 3 = 3x − 5, so 3 + 5 = 3x − 2x, giving x = 8. Verification: 2(8) + 3 = 19 and 3(8) − 5 = 19, both equal. ✓

questions.question: A coffee kiosk recorded the number of cups sold on five consecutive days as follows — Monday: 50; Tuesday: 60; Wednesday: 40; Thursday: 70; Friday: 80. What is the difference between the highest and the lowest number of cups sold on any single day?
questions.explanation: The highest daily sale is Friday with 80 cups, and the lowest is Wednesday with 40 cups. The difference is 80 − 40 = 40 cups.

questions.question: In a test of maximum 200 marks, a candidate needs 33% to pass. Ramesh scored 72 marks in the test. Did he pass, and by how many marks did he pass or fail?
questions.explanation: Passing marks = 33% of 200 = 66. Ramesh scored 72, which is 72 − 66 = 6 marks more than the pass mark, so he passed by 6 marks.

questions.question: A small factory recorded its annual production of ceramic mugs for three consecutive years: 2022 — 5,000 mugs; 2023 — 6,000 mugs; 2024 — 7,200 mugs. What was the total percentage increase in production from 2022 to 2024?
questions.explanation: Increase over the two years = 7,200 − 5,000 = 2,200 mugs. Percentage increase on the 2022 base = (2,200/5,000) × 100 = 44%. (The year-on-year growth was 20% in 2023 and 20% in 2024, but successive growth must not be simply added — 20% + 20% would wrongly suggest 40%.)

questions.question: The volume of a solid cube is 216 cubic centimetres. What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: If the edge of the cube is a, then a³ = 216, so a = 6 cm. Total surface area = 6a² = 6 × 36 = 216 cm². Interestingly the numerical value equals the volume here, which is the trap the distractors exploit: 108 is half, 324 adds a face, and 432 doubles the value.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and then offers a festival discount of 25% on the marked price. What is his profit or loss percentage on the sale?
questions.explanation: Take cost price = ₹100. Marked price = 100 + 40% = ₹140. Selling price after 25% discount = 140 × 0.75 = ₹105. Profit = 105 − 100 = ₹5, i.e., a 5% profit. The net factor is 1.40 × 0.75 = 1.05, so the common mistake of expecting 40% − 25% = 15% profit is wrong.

questions.question: Statements: All doctors are graduates. All graduates are literate. Conclusions: I. All doctors are literate. II. Some literate persons are doctors. Which of the conclusions logically follow(s)?
options: A) Both conclusions I and II follow
D) Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Since every doctor is a graduate and every graduate is literate, every doctor must be literate, so I follows. Because doctors exist as a non-empty class and all of them are literate, some literate persons are necessarily doctors, so II follows as well. Both conclusions follow.

questions.question: Four friends J, K, L and M are sitting in a row facing north, occupying seats 1 to 4 from left to right. J is at the extreme left. L is immediately to the left of M, and K is immediately to the right of M. Who is sitting second from the left end?
questions.explanation: J occupies seat 1. The chain L–M–K (L immediately left of M, K immediately right of M) must occupy seats 2, 3 and 4 in that order. The arrangement from left to right is J, L, M, K, so the person second from the left is L.

questions.question: If 26 January 2026 falls on a Monday, on which day of the week will 15 August 2026 fall? (2026 is not a leap year.)
questions.explanation: Count the days from 26 January to 15 August 2026: remaining days of January = 5 (27th–31st), February = 28, March = 31, April = 30, May = 31, June = 30, July = 31, August = 15. Total = 5 + 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 15 = 201 days. Since 201 = 28 × 7 + 5, the day advances by 5 weekdays from Monday, giving Saturday.

questions.question: Statement: Every student of Class 12 who appeared in the pre-board examination has passed it. Sahil appeared in the pre-board examination as a student of Class 12. Conclusion: Sahil has passed the pre-board examination. On the basis of the statement alone, the conclusion is:
questions.explanation: The statement asserts that every Class 12 student who appeared has passed, and it is given that Sahil is such a student who appeared. By direct universal application, Sahil must have passed, so the conclusion follows with certainty and is definitely true.

questions.question: At what time between 6 o'clock and 7 o'clock will the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock exactly coincide?
questions.explanation: At 6 o'clock the hour hand is at 180°. The minute hand gains on it at 5.5° per minute (6° − 0.5°). The hands coincide when 5.5 × m = 180, so m = 180/5.5 = 360/11 = 32 8/11 minutes past 6.

questions.question: Five friends A, B, C, D and E live on the five floors of a building, floor 1 (ground) to floor 5 (top), one person per floor. C lives on the top floor. A lives above D but below B, and E lives immediately above A. Who lives on the floor immediately above A's floor?
questions.explanation: C takes floor 5. Among A, B, D, E on floors 1–4: D must be below A, and A below B, with E immediately above A. If A were on floor 3, E would need floor 4 and B would need a floor above 3, which is impossible (floor 4 is taken and floor 5 has C). If A were on floor 1, D could not be below A. Hence the only arrangement is D on 1, A on 2, E on 3, B on 4, C on 5. The person immediately above A (floor 2) is E on floor 3.

questions.question: Six students — M, N, O, P, Q and R — have different heights. M is taller than N but shorter than O. P is taller than O. Q is shorter than N. R is taller than P. Who is the second tallest student?
questions.explanation: From the statements: N < M < O; P > O; Q < N; R > P. Chaining these gives R > P > O > M > N > Q, a complete strict ordering of all six students. R is the tallest and P, being taller than O and everyone else except R, is the second tallest.

questions.question: Which organ of the human body produces the hormone insulin, which regulates blood sugar levels?
questions.explanation: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas; deficiency of insulin causes diabetes mellitus. The liver processes nutrients and stores glycogen, the kidneys filter blood, and the spleen is part of the immune and blood-filtration system.

questions.question: The frequency of a sound wave — that is, the number of complete vibrations it makes per second — is measured in which unit?
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), where 1 Hz equals one cycle per second; humans hear roughly between 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz. The watt measures power, the joule measures energy, and the pascal measures pressure.

questions.question: What is the chemical name of common table salt?
questions.explanation: Common salt is sodium chloride (NaCl), obtained mainly from sea water and rock salt deposits. Sodium carbonate is washing soda, sodium bicarbonate is baking soda, and calcium chloride is a deliquescent salt used as a drying agent and de-icer.

questions.question: Which component of human blood plays the primary role in defending the body against infections?
questions.explanation: White blood cells (leucocytes) are the immune cells that engulf pathogens and produce antibodies against infection. Red blood cells carry oxygen with haemoglobin, platelets help in clotting, and plasma is the fluid medium that transports cells, nutrients and wastes.

questions.question: The ozone layer, which absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation, is located in which layer of the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer lies within the stratosphere, roughly between 15 and 35 kilometres above the Earth's surface, where ozone molecules absorb UV-B and UV-C radiation. The troposphere is the lowest weather-bearing layer, while the mesosphere and thermosphere lie far above the ozone layer.

questions.question: Eutrophication — the excessive growth of algae in lakes and ponds that depletes oxygen and kills aquatic life — is primarily caused by the runoff of which nutrients into water bodies?
questions.explanation: Eutrophication is driven mainly by nitrogen and phosphorus, which enter water bodies from chemical fertilisers, sewage and detergents. These nutrients trigger algal blooms; when the algae die and decompose, dissolved oxygen falls sharply, suffocating fish and other aquatic organisms.

questions.question: A patient suffering from high fever and severe joint pain is diagnosed with a viral infection. The doctor explains that the disease is spread by the day-biting Aedes aegypti mosquito, not by the common house-dwelling Culex. Which disease has the patient most likely contracted?
questions.explanation: Dengue is caused by the dengue virus and is spread by the day-biting Aedes aegypti mosquito; high fever with severe joint and muscle pain is its classic presentation. Malaria is a protozoan (Plasmodium) disease spread by the female Anopheles mosquito, filariasis is caused by parasitic worms spread mainly by Culex mosquitoes, and kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is spread by the sandfly — none of these is viral or Aedes-borne.
